knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Compiler graph transformations can fail to preserve eager semantics for special floating-point values
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Graph-level optimizations and backend code generation may assume ordinary finite inputs and therefore mishandle non-finite values or values that overflow to non-finite during lowered execution.

risk_dimensions.shape: Any shape; include scalar and multi-dimensional floating-point tensors
risk_dimensions.dtype: Floating-point dtypes, especially float32 and dtypes prone to overflow to non-finite values
risk_dimensions.device: CPU and other backends reachable through compiler transformations
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Compiled execution paths, optimization levels, and backend dispatch states

failure_mechanism.description: Backend code generation may lower operations into kernels that do not correctly handle non-finite inputs, causing compiled outputs to diverge from eager reference outputs.

input_exploration: Explore floating-point tensors containing +inf, -inf, and NaN
Explore large finite values that may overflow to non-finite under preceding numerical operations
Vary shapes including scalar, 1D, and multi-dimensional tensors
Vary compiler optimization levels and backend configurations
constraint_awareness: Eager execution semantics serve as the reference for numerical outputs
Non-finite propagation and NaN locations must be preserved under graph transformations
Use NaN-aware comparison when expected outputs may contain NaN
oracle_strategy: Compare compiled outputs against eager outputs using exact or NaN-aware assertions
Flag mismatches in non-finite value presence or location

transferability.reason: This knowledge applies to any elementwise or activation API whose eager numerical semantics must be preserved by graph compilers, especially for special floating-point values.

important_considerations: Target activation and elementwise operations that may be fused or lowered by compilers
Inject special floating-point values and overflow-prone finite values
Run candidates under both eager and compiled execution paths
Check that non-finite output locations match the reference
generation_strategy: Create a generic fuzzing harness that selects floating-point tensors, seeds them with special or overflow-prone values, applies an activation or elementwise operation under compiled execution, and compares against eager results with NaN-aware assertions.
